desc:
Count the non-empty substrings of the lowercase string s in which every letter that appears at all appears exactly k times. Letters that do not occur in the substring are not constrained. Substrings are counted by start and end position.

s = "aabbcc", k = 2
aa, bb, cc, aabb, bbcc, aabbcc  -> 6
result = 6
s = "abab", k = 1
a, b, a, b, ab, ba, ab -> 7   ("aba" has two a's)
result = 7
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Enumerating all substrings is O(n<sup>2</sup>) substrings with counting on top. Use the structure of valid substrings: how long can one be?
If a valid substring has d different letters, its length must be exactly d * k. There are only 26 possible values of d.
For each d from 1 to 26, slide a window of fixed length d * k and track how many letters currently have a count of exactly k. The window is valid exactly when that number equals d.
editorial: A valid substring with d distinct letters, each used k times, has length d · k. Since there are at most 26 letters, there are at most 26 candidate window lengths (and only those with d · k ≤ n matter). For each length, slide a fixed window over the string.

Maintain the 26 letter counts and eq, the number of letters whose count is exactly k. When a count moves from k - 1 to k, eq grows; when it moves from k to k + 1, eq shrinks, and the reverse transitions apply when letters leave. A window of length d · k is valid iff eq == d: then d letters already account for all d · k positions, so nothing else can be inside. Total time O(26 · n), space O(1).
